node_definition.done_when:
All of the following hold at the committed head. (1) A package reckon/crew/picker/ renders Jev's state and questions from Jinja templates in reckon/crew/picker/templates/, following the loader pattern of imas_codex/llm/prompt_loader.py as recorded in the reuse map, with jinja2 declared as a direct dependency in pyproject.toml and uv.lock (it is already installed transitively, so the shared environment is not re-synced). (2) The templates inject, per candidate backend, only these live facts: availability or serving state, window utilisation, burn multiple, pace allowance and reset time from the budget view, local-lane worker slots and congestion from lane.json, and recent outcome counts over 14 days from the ledger for the same role and spec level; plus the node's role, spec level, capability requirements, goal, done-when, estimated context and the orchestrator's free-form comment verbatim. A test asserts the rendered state for a representative node is at most 1,500 tokens (4 characters per token). (3) A candidate filter in code removes, each with a recorded reason: models refused by the account (codex-spark), backends held on budget, metered backends whose burn multiple exceeds budget.pace_multiple, and nodes that do not fit the context window; and an exact-level node routes to the local lane without asking Jev whenever the local lane reports at least one worker slot. (4) Jev is called by POST to https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions with model typesafe/jev-1.13, the request shape scripts/jev_probe.py and docs/evidence/fragments/one-typesafe-model-picker/jev-call-probe.html established, reading answers.ID.choice, answers.ID.confidence and answers.ID.probabilities for each question id ID, with the key read from OPENROUTER_API_KEY_RECKON or reckon's .env, a 10 s timeout, and the Jev model id recorded on every selection. (5) Below a confidence threshold (0.6 for a metered pick, 0.4 for the local lane) or on any Jev error, the selection falls back to flight default_backend and records fallback_reason; it never falls back silently. (6) reckon crew pick --project P --role R --spec-level L --goal G --done-when W [--comment C] prints one JSON selection naming backend, family, model, effort, the option probabilities, confidence, jev model id, fallback_reason, offered and excluded candidates with reasons, rendered token estimate and latency, and dispatches nothing. (7) reckon crew pick --replay 50 runs the 50 most recent ledger dispatches through the live picker, and the fragment docs/evidence/fragments/one-typesafe-model-picker/picker-prototype.html publishes its table (actual backend and outcome beside picked backend and confidence) and summary (agreement rate, picks of a refused model which must be 0, fallback rate, median latency), plus a design note naming every question with its type, instructions and criteria, the state schema, the filter, the thresholds, the fallback, the pinned Jev model id and the credential path. (8) tests/test_picker.py passes with Jev mocked, covering the filter exclusions, the exact-to-local rule, the token bound, and fallback on an unreachable Jev and on low confidence.
 (9) The candidate snapshot reuses, rather than reimplements, the functions the reuse map names (read it with: git -C /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/.reckon-worktrees/reckon-c8f839407e49/s25-picker/picker-reuse-map show 5b767974c:docs/evidence/fragments/one-typesafe-model-picker/picker-reuse-map.html): reckon.budget state_for and group_pace for utilisation, burn and allowance; reckon.crew.lane_document read_lane_document and read_lane_admission for local-lane room; reckon.crew.resumption probe_lane_availability for serving state; reckon.crew.routing _context_fit_verdict and _competence_verdict as hard filters; and templates render under jinja2 StrictUndefined as in render_prompt_strict, so a missing live fact raises rather than rendering empty. The picker returns an existing backend name; it does not yet change plan_dispatch.
